courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Discrete Structures
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Logic, proof techniques, sets, basic counting rules, relations, functions and recursion. Graphs and trees.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, CS minor, or Cyber Security minor; and eligibility for MAT 1140 or C or better in: MAT 1050 or MAT 1052 , and MAT 1060 ; MAT 1140 ; MAT 1150 ; or MAT 2140 .

courses.title: Introduction to Programming and Problem Solving
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Problem-solving methods. Object-oriented concepts including classes, inheritance, and polymorphism. Basic control structures and data types. Files. Input/Output. Exception handling. Program documentation and testing.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, CS minor, or Cyber Security minor; and eligibility for MAT 1140 or C or better in: MAT 1050 or MAT 1052, and MAT 1060 ; MAT 1140 ; MAT 1150 ; or MAT 2140 .

courses.title: Data Structures and Advanced Programming
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Abstract data types and their implementation using linear and non-linear data structures. Interfaces and generics. Recursive structures and operations. Big-O notation and introduction to algorithm analysis. Introduction to GenAI and its ethical use. GenAI-assisted programming.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, CS minor, or Cyber Security minor; and C or better in the following: CS 1400 ; CS 1300 ; and MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , or MAT 2140 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Systems Programming
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Fundamentals of C programming and Unix environment. File management, communications and process control. Regular expressions. Unix system calls, concurrent and socket programming.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or Cyber Security minor, and C or better in CS 1280 or CS 1400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Cyber Security and Network Communications
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of cyber security and authentication systems. Fundamentals of network architecture, communication technologies and protocols. Client-server model and socket programming. Basic network attacks and defense mechanisms. Fundamentals of secure programming and web security. Basics of incident response and digital forensics. Overview of risk management and cyber law.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or Cyber Security minor, and C or better in CS 2600 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computer Organization and Assembly Programming
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Number representation, integer arithmetic. Von Neumann machine. Instruction set architecture. Addressing modes. Assembly programming. Arrays and records. Subroutines and macros. Interrupts. I/O interfacing and communication.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1300 and CS 1400 .

courses.title: Numerical Methods and Computing
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Linear algebra concepts, Linear Transformations and Matrix Factorizations, Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors, Least Squares, error analysis, floating-point representations, roots of non-linear equations, systems of linear equations, interpolation, numerical integration.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, and C or better in CS 2400 and MAT 1150 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Formal Languages and Automata
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Finite automata. Non-determinism. Regular expressions and languages. Context-free grammars and push down automata. Ambiguity. Closure properties. Normal forms. Context-free and non-context-free languages.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Algorithms for fundamental problems. Efficiency analysis using asymptotic notation. Principal algorithm design techniques and their tradeoffs. NP-theory and approaches used to address intractability.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 and STA 2260 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Object-Oriented Design and Programming
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Elements of the object model. Abstraction, encapsulation, modularity, hierarchy and polymorphism. UML Modeling. Object-oriented design principles. Design patterns. Implementation and programming of system design. Code generation. Overview of advanced file and database technology. Model integration with database. Introduction to embedded software. Object and portable data. Comprehensive examples using a case study approach.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Logic design and computer arithmetic. Logical properties of flip-flops and sequential machines. Datapath and control unit design. Pipelining. Memory hierarchy and storage technology. Multiprocessing and alternative architectures.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2640 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computers and Society
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 4C or 5D] Impact of computing technology on individuals and on society. Various current uses of computing devices, how these have evolved, and what the future might bring. Benefits and dangers of information technology. How the Internet and computing devices have fundamentally changed the way we work, play, and interact with others. Overview of computer and information technology (e.g., networking and communications, information management). Secure computing principles and practice. Consequent rise of new social, legal and diversity issues, making it essential for everyone to acquire a working understanding of the role of this technology in our daily lives. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Concepts of Programming Languages
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Concepts in programming languages. Virtual machines and abstraction. Syntax and semantics. Declarations and types. Scoping and binding. Data abstraction. Control and abstraction. Subprograms and implementations. Exception handling. Programming paradigms.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, C or better in CS 3110 , and C or better in CS 2640 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Overview of operating systems. Operating system structures. Process management. Concurrency and synchronization. Deadlock. Processor management. Operating system security. Scheduling and dispatch. Memory management. Virtual memory. Device management. File systems.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, and C or better in CS 3650 and STA 2260 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Technical presentations by students on current developments in computer science. Essays on seminar topics.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and senior standing.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Models of the software development process and metrics. Software requirements and specifications. Methodologies, tools and environments. Human-computer interaction. Software architecture, design and implementation techniques. Project management. Cost estimation. Testing and validation. Secure software development life cycle and common software security issues. Automated build, deployment and continuous integration. Maintenance and evolution.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 2] Integration techniques including integration by parts, integrals of trigonometric products, partial fractions, substitution and trigonometric substitution. Hyperbolic functions. Improper Integrals, sequences and series, polar coordinates, parametric equations and conic sections.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB >=3, AP Calc BC >=3, or C or better in MAT 1140 or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Introduction to Newtonian Mechanics
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to mechanics, including Newton’s laws, vectors, statics, kinematics, conservation laws, rotational motion, Newtonian gravity, fluids, and simple harmonic motion. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ( MAT 1150 can be concurrent).

courses.title: Newtonian Mechanics Laboratory
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments in Newtonian mechanics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Probability and Statistics for Computer Scientists and Engineers
courses.requirement: Major Required: 71 units
courses.description: Descriptive statistics. Rules of probability. Discrete and continuous probability distributions. Sampling distributions. Large- and small-sample inferences for one- and two-sample points. Interval Estimation and hypothesis testing for means, proportions and variances. Chi-Square tests. Analysis of variance. Introduction to regression and correlation.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1310 .

courses.title: Symbolic Programming
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Languages for processing symbolic data with emphasis on applications in artificial intelligence.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Parallel Processing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: The taxonomy of concurrent and parallel systems. Communication and synchronization, multicomputer and multiprocessor systems. Shared-memory and message passing programming paradigms. Parallel problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor; and C or better in CS 3310 ; or consent of instrucor.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Network architectures and standards. Layers and protocols. Circuit switching, packet switching and routing. Client-server concepts. Network security. Web programming.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or Cyber Security minor, and C or better in CS 2610 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Compilers and Interpreters
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Interpreter and compiler structures. Lexical analysis. Symbol tables. Syntax analysis and parsing techniques. Syntax-directed translation. Run-time environments. Intermediate code generation and optimization. Compiler development tools.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3110 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Introduction to natural language processing with emphasis on foundational methods. Topics include lexical, syntactic, and basic semantic analysis; statistical algorithms and classical machine learning models for language representation and modeling; introductory word embeddings and applied use of NLP libraries. Case studies include sentiment analysis, text classification, and chatbots.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science major and CS 3010 ; or Data Science, Computational Linguistics, or Artificial Intelligence minor and C or better in CS 2410 .

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CS 5190 Core principles of computer vision, focusing on image formation, representation, and feature extraction as the basis for visual understanding. Theoretical foundations include camera models, geometric reasoning, illumination, and feature learning. Modern approaches extend these principles with convolutional networks and transformer-based models for recognition, detection, and interpretation across diverse domains
courses.prerequisites: CS major or AI minor; and C or better in CS 3010 , or MAT 2240 and CS 2410 .

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Overview of the different application areas of AI. Introduction to the basic AI concepts and techniques such as heuristic search, knowledge representation, automated reasoning. In-depth discussion of several AI application areas: their specific problems, tools and techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; or Data Science/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 .

courses.title: Machine Learning and Its Applications
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Supervised learning techniques, including linear models for regression, linear models for classification, decision trees, support vector machines, neural networks. Unsupervised learning techniques, including clustering and dimensionality reduction. Related advanced topics. Case studies and applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3010 ; Data Science minor/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; Cybersecurity minor and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Graphics Processing Unit Computing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Programming massively parallel processors on Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). Heterogeneous data parallel computing, multidimensional grids and data, compute architecture and scheduling, memory architecture and data locality, performance considerations, parallel patterns, and advanced patterns and applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, and C or better in CS 2600 and CS 2640 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Social Computing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Representing, modeling, processing and analyzing social information. Graph based techniques for social network analysis, community detection, influence spread and centrality analysis. Models for application domains such as social media, epidemiology, and political science. Parallel and distributed tools for large scale modeling and analysis.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Software for Intelligent Robotics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CS 5240 Design and development of software systems for intelligent robotics. Emphasis on software architectures, algorithms, and frameworks that enable robotic autonomy. Topics include robot control paradigms and behavior design, perception and sensing pipelines, and software approaches for navigation, planning, localization, and mapping.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or minor, and C or better in CS 2400 or CS 3310 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Web Search and Recommender Systems
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Web Search engine architectures, techniques, and technologies. Web crawling. Web document processing, Link analysis, and ranking. Introduction to retrieval models. Search engine optimization. Web search user interfaces. Recommender Systems. Evaluation. Current trends.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ Artificial Intelligence/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence - Theory and Applications
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Core principles of generative deep learning. Predictive vs. generative paradigms. Modern architecture includes GANs, VAEs, transformers, and large language models with applications across domains.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or AI minor; and C or better in CS 3010 , or MAT 2250 and CS 2410 .

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Database and transaction systems. Database components. Database design and constraints. Normalization theory. Data modeling. Relational and object data models. Relational algebra and calculus. SQL programming paradigms. Concurrency control, crush recovery, and security.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Mining
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: An end-to-end view of data mining, covering data acquisition, preparation, and analysis using various algorithms. Explore data types, attributes, storage, and perform exploratory data analysis with statistical techniques and visualization. Topics include pattern mining, clustering, classification, and outlier detection. Ethical considerations and applications of data mining are also discussed.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ ArtificiaI Intelligence/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Basic concepts in 2D and 3D graphics. Graphics hardware. Drawing concepts in 2D and 3D graphics. Geometric transformations. Windowing and clipping algorithms. Simple hidden line and surface removal. Color models and applications. 3D modeling. Animation. OpenGL libraries.
courses.prerequisites: CS major; and C or better in CS 241 or CS 2400 , and CS 256 or CS 2560 .

courses.title: Computability
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Abstract models of computation, including Turing machines. Church-Turing thesis. Decidability. Intractable problems. Theoretical and practical capabilities and limitations of computing machines.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3110 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cryptography and Information Security
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Information security fundamentals. Symmetric and asymmetric encryption. Digital signatures and certificates. Applications of cryptography.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, CS minor, or Cyber Security minor; and C or better in CS 2610 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Big Data Analytics and Cloud Computing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Data analytics lifecycle. Data analytics methods. Cloud infrastructure. Cloud storage, computing models and architectures. Big data and cloud security. Case studies.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cloud Computing Practicum with Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Intro to Cloud Architecture and Amazon Web Services (AWS) Platform, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Microsoft Azure. AWS Networking and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3). Amazon Elastic Computing (E3B/C2). Databases on AWS, GCP and Azure. Identity and Access Management (IAM) in AWS. Deploying Cloud Application on AWS, GCP and Azure.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Prompt Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to prompt engineering, focusing on designing effective prompts for Large Language Models (LLMs). Students will explore essential concepts, including LLM foundations, interactive prompts, and parameter tuning. Various prompt patterns and templates, customization and fine-tuning techniques, and methods for evaluating prompt effectiveness are covered. Ethical considerations and security aspects in prompt engineering will also be discussed. Additionally, learn to apply prompt engineering in specialized domains through hands-on development, gaining practical experience in building AI-powered applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major/ CS minor/ Cybersecurity minor and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ Computational Linguistic/ AI minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: An in-depth understanding of how data analytics techniques can be applied to identify, understand, and respond to cybersecurity threats using Gen AI. Various data analytics methods and tools that are used to detect, analyze, and mitigate cybersecurity threats. Topics covered include Gen AI, data preprocessing, anomaly detection, intrusion detection, threat intelligence analysis, and predictive modeling. Practical hands-on experience will be emphasized through lab exercises and real-world case studies using Gen AI.
courses.prerequisites: CS major/minor or Cybersecurity minor, and C or better in CS 2610 ; or Data Science Minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Game Development
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Overview of game development processes. Game programming topics including: languages and architectures, mathematics, collision detection, physics, graphics, animation, artificial intelligence (AI), and audio.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Mobile Application Development
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Mobile development environments and fundamentals. Mobile user interface (UI) design and implementation. Mobile data storage and management. Network programming in mobile and integration with cloud services. Advanced mobile development with external sensors, libraries and frameworks. Hands-on mobile development practices and the distribution of mobile applications. Mobile application security.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400; or consent of instructor. Recommmended that students should already have a familiarity with Java, an understanding of basic object oriented programming (OOP), studied basic algorithms and data structures.

courses.title: Software Engineering Practice
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Team and project-oriented software engineering. Practice in the hands-on process of software production and quality control. Documentation and management methods for analysis, design, implementation and testing phases of software production. Survey and usage of agile development methodologies and tools. Software engineering security issues.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, and C or better in CS 4350 and CS 4800 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-21 units
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Introduction to Web Science and Technology
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: Overview of Internet and World Wide Web history, standards, technologies, and practices. Introduction to Web application development. Introduction to best practices and current topics in Web Science, Design, and Development, such as Web Usability, Web Security, Web Search, Online Social Networks, and Semantic Web.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1260 , CS 1280 , or CS 1400 ; OR consent of instructor.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Data Science
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: Foundations of data science. Critical concepts and skills in mathematics, statistics and computer programming for data analytics. Fundamental data and file structures to support data analytics. Analysis of real-world datasets. Data privacy and data security.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1400 , or Data Science/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 1260 ; MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; and STA 1200 , STA 1202 , STA 1300 , STA 2100 , or STA 2260 .

courses.title: User Interface Design and Programming
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: User interfaces. Interaction design and development process. Usability of interactive systems. Graphical User Interface programming. GUI components and controls. Event-handling. User evaluation methods.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 1400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Python for Programmers
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: Python basics. Data structures and control structures. Functions and functional forms. Objects, classes, inheritance, and polymorphism. I/O and exceptions. Advanced features.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1400 or CS 1280 ; Data Science minor, AI Minor or Computational Linguistics Minor and C or better in MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; or Cyber Security minor and C or better in CS 1400 .

courses.title: C++ Programming
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: C++ fundamentals. Recursion, structures, class encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and exception handling. Memory management using pointers. Template functions and template classes. Software reuse and object-oriented programming.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1280 or CS 1400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-3 units
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-3 units
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Internship in Computer Science
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-3 units
courses.description: On-the-job training and work experience in the Computer Science. The internship is arranged by the student and may not be a continuation of an ongoing job or volunteer experience. A minimum of 4 hours per week (60 hours/semester) per unit credit. Student must be enrolled in CS 4410 during the term in which work at the internship site is done. Hours worked in one term may not carry over into another. Total credit limited to 2 units, but may be repeated as appropriate.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units, but may be repeated as appropriate.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-3 units
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Projects typical of problems which graduates must solve in their fields of employment. Project results are presented in a formal report.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-3 units
courses.description: Continuation of a project under faculty supervision with expectation of full project completion by the end of the term. Projects typical of problems which graduates must solve in their fields of employment. Project results are presented in a formal report.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.

courses.title: Computer Science Project Practicum
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-3 units
courses.description: Selection and completion of a Computer Science hands-on project under faculty supervision. Team projects. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2400 or CS 2410 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units, with a maximum of 2 units per semester.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.requirement: Summer Sponsored Experience: 0 unit
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
